Facts: On Oct 16 2000, defendant Song and others went to collect engineering payment. They had a conflict with victim Yang. They insulted him, then later Yang with a combat knife found them, they fought. Dong used a bench to hit Yang's head/back, Song used a short knife to stab Yang's back, Li used a pointed knife to stab Yang's waist. Yang died from kidney artery rupture due to sharp force. So participants used knives, causing death. This is homicide. Likely "故意杀人罪" (intentional homicide). Need to see if there is premeditation? They attacked after being insulted. They used knives, causing death. So they committed intentional homicide. Also possibly "聚众斗殴致人死亡罪"? Under Chinese law, there is "聚众斗殴致人死亡罪" (article 293). But the participants are a group of five, they engaged in a fight. However they used knives, which is more serious. The law: If a group of people gather to fight and cause death, can be charged with "聚众斗殴致人死亡罪". Also "故意伤害致死罪"? Actually "故意伤害致死" is also a crime. But the act is intentional killing? They used knives to stab, likely intent to kill. So "故意杀人罪". Could also be "非法持有、使用刀具"? Not a crime. So answer: [罪名]故意杀人罪<eoa>.

But need to consider multiple crimes: maybe "非法拘禁"? No. "抢劫"? No. "寻衅滋事"? Could be "寻衅滋事罪" for provoking. But the main is homicide. The question: "只写这部分事实直接支持的罪名". The fact includes that they used knives to stab and cause death. So homicide. Also "聚众斗殴致人死亡罪" is supported because they were a group fighting. Which is more appropriate? Chinese criminal law: Article 293: "聚众斗殴致人重伤、死亡的，处三年以上七年以下有期徒刑". However if the act is intentional homicide, article 232: "故意杀人". The prosecution may choose either. The fact says they attacked with knives, likely intent to kill. So "故意杀人罪". Could also be "故意伤害致死罪" (article 234) if they intended to cause injury but caused death. But they used knives to stab vital area, likely intent to kill. So "故意杀人罪". Provide single.

Thus final answer: - 单个罪名: [罪名]故意杀人罪<eoa>
